name: Cyprus
summary_text: Cyprus is workable for trans visitors. The legal framework is mid-transition: public incitement to hatred based on gender identity is a criminal offence (2015), and gender identity is an aggravating factor in hate crime (2017). A legal gender recognition bill (self-determination basis) was approved by the Council of Ministers in September 2022 and is pending in parliament; until it passes, LGR requires surgery under the 2002 Civil Registry Law — a resident-facing gap. No traveler-facing restrictions: no bathroom law, no border issues (EU member), tourist infrastructure is Western-standard and accustomed to diverse visitors. Gender identity is not yet an explicit ground in the non-discrimination framework, and the divided island matters: the northern part (de facto Turkish-controlled) has its own LGR regime requiring surgical proof, weaker protections, and less documentation — travelers should treat the north as closer to Turkey's risk profile.

sources.claim_summary: UPR advocacy sheet for Cyprus's 4th cycle (2024) on the situation of LGBTI persons: assesses implementation of cycle-3 recommendations. Notes progress: Law 87(I)/2015 criminalises public incitement to violence or hatred based on sexual orientation or gender identity; Law 31(I)/2017 adds prejudice motivation as an aggravating factor. Outstanding: gender identity not yet a prohibited discrimination ground in equal-treatment legislation, no action plan against homophobia/transphobia, and pending legislation on transgender persons.

European Commission Network of Legal Experts country report on gender equality in Cyprus (2024, reporting period 2023): how EU equality rules are transposed into Cypriot national law, including gender-identity-related aspects of the legal framework.

Queer Cyprus Association presentation for Cyprus's UPR: lists prior recommendations (anti-discrimination, hate-speech criminalisation, victim support, enactment of transgender-persons legislation) and developments, including the 2015 Criminal Code amendment covering SOGI incitement.

Queer Cyprus Association booklet on legal gender recognition (Diversity of Colours project, EU-funded): describes the association's solidarity line (7 days/week, confidential psychosocial, legal and social support for LGBTI+ people on identity, education, work, family, shelter, health, military service), psychologist and legal-expert networks, and LGR issues - covering both the Republic of Cyprus and the north.

ILGA report on SOGIESC recommendations at the 32nd UPR Working Group session (Jan-Feb 2019): includes the Cyprus chapter - summarises SOGIESC remarks, advanced questions and recommendations for Cyprus among 14 states reviewed.

European Commission legal experts' country report on non-discrimination in Cyprus (2020, reporting period 2019): transposition and implementation of the EU equality directives, including SOGI grounds in Cypriot law.

sources.title: Cyprus: Penal code amended to protect against discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Oct 2013): Cyprus amended its penal code to criminalise incitement to violence or hatred based on sexual orientation or gender identity (up to 3 years' imprisonment or €5,000 fine); workplace protections for LGBT people added in 2004.
